verdicts.claim: A checkpoint copies committed frames from the WAL back into the database file. The WAL is reset only after all its content is tran
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: reset happens "if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL"

verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint when the WAL reaches a threshold of 1000 pages ... PASSIVE mode on the thread of the committing connection
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages"; "run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT"; default style PASSIVE

verdicts.claim: The pragma wal_autocheckpoint changes the threshold, and a value of 0 or less disables it.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html (c1-3, mirror): "Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off"; cited c1-1/c1-5 cover threshold only

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE is the default checkpoint mode. It copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers ... syncs only if every frame
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: "Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish"; syncs db only if whole log checkpointed

verdicts.claim: FULL and RESTART wait on the busy handler until no writer is active and readers use the latest snapshot ... block new writers, not readers
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 FULL: "blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer"; "blocks new database writers while it is pending"

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE works like RESTART and also truncates the WAL file to zero bytes just before a successful return. Practitioners run TRUNCATE in low-traffic windows
verdicts.evidence: v2: "truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return"; kunalganglani: run it "during low-traffic windows to shrink WAL"

verdicts.claim: If automatic checkpoints are disabled, nothing stops the WAL from growing without limit. The application must then run checkpoints itself
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "nothing to prevent the WAL file from growing excessively"; "run checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process". kunalganglani does not tie unbounded growth to disabling, so the '(two sources)' label overstates

verdicts.claim: A long-running read transaction prevents the checkpoint from making progress ... no checkpoint completes and the WAL grows without bound
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress"; "the WAL file will grow without bound"

verdicts.claim: Practitioner guidance calls checkpointing a production footgun: a large checkpoint ... can raise p99 latency ... checkpoint on a cadence
verdicts.evidence: kunalganglani (2026-09-15): "Checkpointing is the production footgun"; "p99 goes off a cliff"; "Do not checkpoint on every request". Syncthing post does not discuss latency

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: Syncthing post says truncating the WAL needs exclusive locking, proposes truncation only at multi-gigabyte sizes
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing (2026-02-06): "truncate the WAL would mandate some kind of exclusive locking"; "If the size of the WAL reaches critical levels of multiple gigabytes, we need to act"
